verdict.rationale: OpenClaw is a self-hosted gateway that runs on your own machine. Its memory is kept as plain Markdown files in your local workspace, and you choose your own LLM provider. This architecture implies the vendor does not collect your data, so you can limit training exposure by picking your provider. However, nothing in the evidence addresses model training, and prompts still go to whichever third-party provider you configure. Missing for 10: an explicit no-training policy or data-use statement, a documented training opt-out control, evidence of local or offline model support that keeps data off third-party providers, and independent corroboration.
